pitch.heard_intro: There is no design brief from DMP yet. Everything here comes from what dmp.com publishes in its sitemap and from the SEO and AEO analysis in the portal. Tell us where it is wrong; your words outrank ours.
heard: No stated promise, likes or dislikes yet. The promise line on the home page is ours and is unconfirmed.
DMP is a current Quantum client with a HubSpot CRM, marketing, sales and service launch under way, so the site has to feed that: forms that create records, one place for dealers to start.
Every claim stays tied to dmp.com. Where we could not read it, we said so on the list below instead of guessing.
found: dmp.com earns about 24,493 organic visits a month on 7,462 keywords, but 66 percent of that is people already searching the brand (Semrush, 13 September 2026).
The apex domain answers with a 307, the home page had no title, no H1 and no canonical when crawled, and no robots.txt or sitemap was readable at dmp.com.
DMP appeared in none of nine buyer searches run from Springfield, Missouri, and was named in none of the AI answers.
No schema, no sameAs links, no address and no tappable phone number were found. Authority is not the problem: 1,916 referring domains, Authority Score 39.
There is no blog or insights section, and no page answers a buyer's question in a buyer's words.
The pages that earn the traffic are product and support pages, such as dealer admin, the 734 access module and the control panels index.
pitch.choose_intro: The words and the pages are the same in all three. What differs is the register. Open each one and tell us which feels like DMP.
pick_reasons: The audience is dealers and specifiers
They scan a catalogue to find a panel or a module. Clean puts the product names and categories first and stays out of the way.
dmp.com lists dozens of product pages and a deep resource library. A plain, fast, high-contrast layout carries that better than a showy one.
We have no brand guide yet
Clean makes the fewest assumptions about brand, so DMP's real logo and colours can drop in without a redesign.
pitch.pick_change: Replace the placeholder wordmark and accent with DMP's real logo and colour, which we could not read from dmp.com.
alternatives: The safe, image-led choice: layered, sales-forward, and the one that shows the most photography once DMP supplies its own.
The wildcard: serif and editorial, so a manufacturer reads like an established company.
plan: Serve the site at one canonical host with a 301, publish robots.txt and a sitemap, add titles, one H1 per page and Organization plus LocalBusiness schema.
Confirm the items below, supply the logo and photography, and sign off copy for every product line.
Build the eight product line pages with FAQ markup, Service schema and an enquiry form on each.
Build the Springfield, Missouri page and add sameAs links to LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB and YouTube.
Publish the about, careers and news pages and the first three answer posts on access control, fire alarm and video.
Re-run the same nine Springfield searches, the same six AI questions and the same page audit against the baseline.

search.heading: Where you stand in search today, and what changes

confirm: Everything on dmp.com page by page. www.dmp.com serves pages only after a JavaScript bot challenge, so this run read the sitemap, robots.txt and the portal SEO analysis only. Every page was written from product and category names, not from DMP's own copy. All copy needs DMP review.
The promise. There is no brief from DMP, so the home page line is ours and unconfirmed.
The logo, accent colour and typefaces. The preview uses a plain DMP wordmark and a deep red placeholder accent. Neither comes from DMP.
Legal name, street address and phone number. None were readable, so none appear. The mobile menu shows a "Call" link with no number until the phone is supplied.
The year DMP was founded, staff counts, certifications and awards. None are sourced, so none appear.
Testimonials, partners, team and customer names. None were readable, so none appear.
Product claims. Each product line lists only the names that appear in the sitemap. Specifications, listings and compatibility need DMP's product team.
The industries. Eight of eleven are used. Industrial manufacturing, multi-tenant and residential are left out and can be added.
Whether DMP operates its own monitoring centre, and how dealers should be described.
Social profiles. The SEO analysis names LinkedIn, Crunchbase, BBB, YouTube and Facebook but gives no URLs, so none are linked.
Photography. Every image is a generated stand-in from the Quantum library and is labelled as such.
The 307 on the apex domain and the bot challenge. Confirm with DMP's IT whether the challenge will stay once the new site is live, because it also blocks search crawlers.
pitch.footer: Prepared for Digital Monitoring Products. Nothing here is live or indexed. Photographs are generated stand-ins and labelled as such.
